title: Finding Piecewise Formulas for a Triangular Wave and a Step Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find a piecewise formula for each graphed function: (a) a graph consisting of a line segment from (0, 0) to (1, 1) and a line segment from (1, 1) to (2, 0); (b) a step graph on [0, 4] that equals 2 on [0, 1) and [2, 3), and equals 0 on [1, 2) and [3, 4].
finalAnswer: \text{(a) } f(x) = \begin{cases} x, & 0 \le x \le 1 \\ -x + 2, & 1 < x \le 2 \end{cases}; \quad \text{(b) } f(t) = \begin{cases} 2, & 0 \le t < 1 \text{ or } 2 \le t < 3 \\ 0, & 1 \le t < 2 \text{ or } 3 \le t \le 4 \end{cases}

steps.title: Determine the Two Linear Equations for Graph (a)
steps.mathExpression: m_1 = \frac{1 - 0}{1 - 0} = 1 \implies y = x; \quad m_2 = \frac{0 - 1}{2 - 1} = -1 \implies y - 1 = -1(x - 1) \implies y = -x + 2
steps.explanation: In graph (a), the first segment joins (0, 0) to (1, 1), giving slope 1 and equation y = x on [0, 1]. The second segment joins (1, 1) to (2, 0), giving slope -1 and equation y = -x + 2 on (1, 2].
steps.why: The point-slope formula y - y_1 = m(x - x_1) determines the equation of each linear segment from its endpoints.

steps.title: Identify the Constant Pieces for Graph (b)
steps.explanation: In graph (b), each horizontal segment has a solid dot at its left endpoint and an open circle at its right endpoint (except at t = 4, which has a solid dot at (4, 0)).
steps.why: Solid dots denote inclusion (<=) of the endpoint in that branch, whereas open circles denote strict inequality (<).

steps.title: Assemble the Complete Piecewise Formulas
steps.mathExpression: f(x) = \begin{cases} x, & 0 \le x \le 1 \\ -x + 2, & 1 < x \le 2 \end{cases}, \qquad f(t) = \begin{cases} 2, & 0 \le t < 1 \\ 0, & 1 \le t < 2 \\ 2, & 2 \le t < 3 \\ 0, & 3 \le t \le 4 \end{cases}
steps.explanation: Combine the branch formulas with their respective subintervals to obtain the complete piecewise definitions for (a) and (b).
steps.why: A piecewise function is uniquely specified by listing its formula on each disjoint subinterval of its domain.
